Judge-versus-human confusion matrix

Source: R/confusion.R
confusion.Rd

Shows where a judge and humans disagree. Label order is preserved from label_levels rather than sorted alphabetically.

Usage

confusion(
  x,
  normalize = c("none", "row", "col"),
  label_levels = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  human_col = NULL,
  judge_col = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A yourhonor_calibration object or a ratings data frame holding one human column and one judge column (see human_col and judge_col).

normalize

One of "none", "row", or "col".

label_levels

Complete label universe in display order. A calibration object's stored levels are used by default.

conf_level

Confidence level for exact per-class binomial intervals.

human_col, judge_col

Names of the human and judge columns of a ratings data frame. Both must be given together. When both are NULL, columns named human and judge are used if present; otherwise a data frame with exactly two columns is read as human then judge. A message (class yourhonor_inferred_columns) reports the choice whenever inference ignored columns or read them positionally. Cannot be combined with a calibration object, which carries its own pairing.

Value

A tibble with human_label, judge_label, n, and prop, in label_levels order. The resolved level order is attached as the "label_levels" attribute. Per-class metrics remain attached for compatibility and are also available through confusion_metrics().

Examples

ratings <- data.frame(
  human = c("C", "C", "P", "I"),
  judge = c("C", "P", "P", "I")
)
confusion(ratings, normalize = "row", label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
          human_col = "human", judge_col = "judge")
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   human_label judge_label     n  prop
#>   <chr>       <chr>       <int> <dbl>
#> 1 I           I               1   1  
#> 2 P           I               0   0  
#> 3 C           I               0   0  
#> 4 I           P               0   0  
#> 5 P           P               1   1  
#> 6 C           P               1   0.5
#> 7 I           C               0   0  
#> 8 P           C               0   0  
#> 9 C           C               1   0.5
